generator_view.scenario: A household makes two espresso shots every day and almost always combines them with steamed milk. It is choosing a first repeat-purchase bag from three frozen offers: a one-pound Colombian Santa Barbara whole-bean bag labeled single origin and 100% Arabica at 16.98 dollars, a two-pound Sumatra whole-bean blend labeled 100% Arabica at 15.48 dollars with a 55-percent-of-100 aggregate over twelve reviews, and a 28-dollar instant Arabica/Robusta blend containing yerba mate and garcinia cambogia whose captured page does not state a comparable package amount. The research set also includes general pages about Arabica, Robusta, single-origin labeling, espresso extraction, and a milk-based espresso recipe, plus three community discussions containing repeat-buying, roast-preference disagreement, and sampling advice.
generator_view.target: Help the household choose what to trial and later rebuy for two daily milk-based espresso drinks. Compare the three exact frozen offers and their normalized costs where possible, explain the Arabica/Robusta and single-origin/blend distinctions without treating labels as laboratory proof, distinguish espresso extraction from bean identity, and state what the milk recipe can and cannot establish. Reconcile the individual community experiences at their proper scope. End with a fixed-recipe blinded trial and a conditional lowest-total-cost repeat purchase or deferral, not a universal bean winner.

query_requirements.text: Audit the three exact frozen offers and normalize only comparable costs, preserving seller-label, package-size, format, rating, ingredient, and missing-field boundaries.
Explain general Arabica and Robusta yield, caffeine, production-cost, bitterness, body, and crema context while stating why it does not authenticate or predict an exact frozen product.
Separate geographic single-origin and blend labels from botanical species and from espresso extraction, leaving exact composition, provenance, freshness, and machine fit unresolved unless verified.
Use the milk-drink recipe to hold a comparison constant, but state that the captured material does not prove steamed milk erases bean differences.
Reconcile repeat-buying, roast-preference disagreement, and sampling or freshness advice as individual community reports rather than population evidence or results for the frozen bags.

Give an operational small-quantity blinded fixed-recipe multi-day milk-espresso trial with verification, thresholds, stop conditions, total cost, and a conditional lowest-cost rebuy or defer, not a universal bean winner.

research_subgoals.description: Audit exact offer fields, normalize the one- and two-pound costs, and preserve the instant herbal product's missing comparable package amount and format boundary.
Explain the general Arabica and Robusta mechanism and production tradeoffs without transferring them to the identity, ratio, caffeine dose, or cup result of an exact seller product.
Separate single-origin and blend geography, Arabica and Robusta species, and espresso extraction while preserving label-authentication and machine-fit gaps.
Define a fixed milk-based espresso recipe and determine why no captured concept page establishes sensory erasure across the candidate products.
Scope long-term rebuys, direct taste disagreement, sampling, and freshness preferences to individual community authors and turn them into trial-design questions rather than population conclusions.
Synthesize the offer, species, label, extraction, milk-recipe, and community branches into a reversible repeated household trial and conditional lowest-total-cost rebuy or defer.

accepted_phrases: Audit the three seller pages at exact frozen scope. SKU B09DR7Q1RF is titled as a one-pound Colombian Santa Barbara single-origin, medium-roast, whole-bean, 100-percent-Arabica bag at 16.98 dollars. SKU B01L9YE808 is titled as a two-pound Copper Moon Sumatra whole-bean dark-roast blend at 15.48 dollars with a 55-percent-of-100 aggregate over twelve reviews, and its table marks the displayed products 100-percent Arabica. Their nominal costs are 16.98 and 7.74 dollars per pound, subject to exact-style verification. SKU B00A7IIOPI is 28 dollars and seller-described as an instant Arabica and Robusta blend with yerba mate and garcinia cambogia, but the captured page has no comparable package amount. Leave its unit cost, species ratio, dose count, health efficacy, and ordinary whole-bean comparability unresolved, and keep every composition, origin, flavor, freshness, and quality statement at seller scope.

Run a reversible fixed-recipe household trial. First verify exact SKU and selected style, package amount, whole-bean or instant format, ingredient list, species and origin label, roast or production date when present, seller, delivered price, shipping, and return or small-bag option. Exclude the herbal instant product if ordinary whole-bean espresso or its added ingredients are incompatible with the household. Compare admissible candidates in small quantities using one machine, water, basket, dose, grind-tuning procedure, beverage yield, shot-time range, milk type and amount, milk temperature and texture, cup order, blinding, and multiple-day repeats. Predeclare thresholds for dial-in effort, consistency, taste through milk, bitterness, body, aroma, aftertaste, caffeine comfort, waste, and cost per acceptable drink. A result applies only to the tested exact product and recipe; one tasting, changed variables, or an unresolved material field requires another trial or deferral.

The packet supplies three seller offer snapshots, general species and label concepts, a preparation and milk-recipe definition, and individual community experiences, but it does not authenticate every exact product field or contain a completed blinded fixed-recipe household milk-espresso trial.

The 28-dollar Arabica and Robusta product is an instant herbal blend with a missing comparable package amount, so it is not a like-for-like ordinary whole-bean espresso bag until format, ingredients, ratio, and unit cost are verified.
The two-pound blend has the lowest nominal comparable cost per pound, but a larger bag can increase commitment, staling, and waste if it fails the household's milk-drink or workflow thresholds.

Single origin, blend, Arabica, Robusta, and espresso labels describe different claimed axes and do not independently guarantee exact composition, provenance, freshness, machine fit, or milk-drink quality.
A blinded repeated fixed-recipe trial can reduce uncertainty for this household and exact product, but it does not establish a universal species, origin format, roast, or future-batch winner.

Rebuy the lowest total-cost exact coffee candidate that passes verified label, format, ingredient, freshness, fixed-recipe milk-drink taste, caffeine, workflow, waste, and budget thresholds across repeated blinded trials; otherwise buy smaller samples or defer, with no universal species or origin-format winner.

Defer while exact product identity, comparable total cost, ingredient fit, freshness, or repeated fixed-recipe household results remain unresolved, and later rebuy only the least costly exact candidate that passes every predeclared gate.

Do not name a universal Arabica, Robusta, single-origin, or blend winner and do not claim that milk erases the differences. Report the one-pound single-origin offer at 16.98 dollars per pound and the two-pound Sumatra blend at a nominal 7.74 dollars per pound, while keeping both products' identity and quality claims at seller scope. Treat the 28-dollar instant herbal Arabica and Robusta product as incomparable to ordinary whole-bean espresso until package amount, species ratio, ingredients, and format fit are verified. Use general species, origin-label, extraction, recipe, and community material only within their stated boundaries. Verify the exact products and run a small blinded fixed-recipe multi-day milk-espresso trial. Rebuy the lowest total-cost exact candidate that repeatedly clears the household's taste, caffeine, workflow, waste, ingredient, and budget thresholds, use a smaller benchmark when useful, or defer when no candidate clears every gate.

Use the cappuccino material only to define a controlled milk-based espresso recipe. It describes an espresso drink with steamed milk and foam and gives a traditional equal-parts example, while the espresso page defines pressure extraction and concentrated suspended and dissolved solids. Neither page reports a comparison of these bags or says milk erases species, roast, origin, blend, aroma, bitterness, or body. Hold dose, grind procedure, beverage yield, shot time, milk type, amount, temperature, texture, and serving order constant, then test the claimed masking rather than treating it as established.

Keep geography, botany, composition, and extraction as different axes. The single-origin page defines one known geographic origin but says the term may cover one farm, multiple farms, or an entire country and lacks universal label enforcement. Arabica and Robusta are botanical species. Blend does not by itself disclose species or every origin, and a single-origin label does not prove Arabica purity. Espresso is a pressure-based preparation method using finely ground coffee, not a bean species. Therefore single origin, blend, 100-percent Arabica, Arabica and Robusta, or espresso on a seller page does not by itself authenticate composition, exact provenance, freshness, machine fit, or superior milk-drink taste.

Keep the community evidence at author and context scope. The Massachusetts thread contains buy-again lists, one almost-fifteen-year daily custom-blend report, and one exclusive go-to statement. The New Haven thread combines a dark-roast preference, pleasant medium-roast surprises, enthusiastic endorsements, and a direct negative view of the same roaster. The Rhode Island thread contains a sampling plan and one person's medium-dark, lower-oil, and freshness preferences for espresso. These reports motivate repeatability, small samples, freshness checks, and household-specific taste testing; they are not controlled comparisons, population rates, reviews of the three frozen offers, or universal evidence that one species, origin format, roast, or roaster wins.

Use the species pages as general mechanism context only. The Robusta page reports higher crop yield and caffeine, lower production cost, commonly stronger body and bitterness, and a possible body and crema role for good-quality Robusta in traditional Italian espresso blends. The Arabica page describes Robusta as less acidic, more bitter, and more highly caffeinated and discusses Arabica cultivation and labeling. These general statements do not authenticate the exact contents, species ratio, roast, freshness, dose caffeine, crema, extraction behavior, or cup quality of any frozen seller product. Preserve the exact seller labels and leave unverified fields unresolved.
